title: Custom Forward-Backward VJPs for DFA-Guided Diffusion Language Models: An Empirical Study

contributions.purpose: Accelerate gradient computation of DFA acceptance probability in DFA-guided diffusion, which accounts for 57-59% of each guided step.
contributions.mechanism: Custom forward-backward vector-Jacobian products (VJPs) for DFA acceptance probability implemented with Triton kernels, adaptive dispatch, and pre-allocated buffers, avoiding autograd tape storage.
contributions.evaluation: Produces numerically identical gradients to baseline autograd (cosine similarity 1.0, relative L2 error 1.7e-5).
contributions.domain: DFA-guided diffusion language models / constrained text generation
contributions.source_quote: We implement custom forward-backward VJPs for DFA acceptance probability with Triton kernels and adaptive dispatch, producing numerically identical gradients to autograd (cosine similarity 1.0, relative L2 error 1.7 x 10^-5).

contributions.purpose: Measure the end-to-end speedup of the custom VJP approach.
contributions.mechanism: Benchmarking across constraint types and batch sizes against torch.compile baselines.
contributions.evaluation: Evaluated on 4 constraint types x 2 batch sizes, finding limited speedups (1.01-1.23x) that fall short of the 3x target.
contributions.domain: GPU kernel optimization for constrained diffusion decoding
contributions.source_quote: We evaluate on 4 constraint types x 2 batch sizes, finding limited speedups (1.01-1.23x) that fall short of our 3x target.

contributions.purpose: Explain why the custom VJP fails to achieve the targeted speedup.
contributions.mechanism: Analysis of tokenizer-aligned DFA structure (edge counts vs state counts).
contributions.evaluation: Root cause: tokenizer-aligned DFAs have 65K-348K edges despite only 6-68 states, making transition matrices effectively fully dense and invalidating the sparse optimization hypothesis.
contributions.domain: DFA structure analysis for tokenizer-aligned automata
contributions.source_quote: We identify the root cause: tokenizer-aligned DFAs have 65K-348K edges despite only 6-68 states, making transition matrices effectively fully dense.

contributions.purpose: Guide future work away from gradient-computation optimizations for this problem.
contributions.mechanism: Documenting the negative result and recommending alternative directions.
contributions.evaluation: Suggests state-space reduction or approximate inference may be more promising than gradient computation optimizations.
contributions.source_quote: We document this negative result to inform future optimization efforts, suggesting that alternative approaches such as state-space reduction or approximate inference may be more promising.

self_declared_provenance.quote: We hypothesize that custom forward-backward vector-Jacobian products (VJPs) can accelerate DFA-guided diffusion by analytically computing gradients without autograd tape storage.

Our work builds on these foundations by implementing custom VJPs for DFA acceptance probability computation, though we find that the dense structure of tokenizer-aligned DFAs limits the achievable speedups.

The forward-backward algorithm for computing gradients through finite-state computations has a rich history in structured prediction. Eisner (2016) establishes the connection between inside-outside algorithms and backpropagation.

notes: EXPLICIT NEGATIVE-RESULT PAPER: the custom VJP achieves only 1.01-1.23x speedup, far below the 3x target; the paper's core hypothesis (sparse edge-list optimization) is invalidated because tokenizer-aligned DFAs are effectively dense. Framed as an empirical study documenting a negative result.
